speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; can you tell me if this rash is itchy or if you have noticed any skin peeling?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (Incomplete/Atypical). The timeline of fever followed by a facial rash sparing the perioral area, combined with a pruritic rash, is highly suggestive. While the classic "strawberry tongue" or conjunctivitis are absent, the clinical picture warrants immediate evaluation for coronary artery aneurysms. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, CRP, ESR, Liver Function Tests, and Echocardiogram. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and Echocardiogram.
